utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has noticed that Mr. Milan Simic is not in the courtroom. Can we hear from the Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We have been just talking to our client over the phone, and he advised us that he is willing to waive his right for the cross-examination of this witness but would like to be present when the new witness comes in. So in other words, that means we can finish the cross-examination of this witness and then see if he would be able to come today at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So the cross-examination will proceed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I'm Novak Lukic, attorney at law. On behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, I shall be putting a few questions to you. I have to tell you about an impression of mine straight away. During your examination by the Prosecutor and by my colleague Mr. Zecevic, I realised that you were aware of many details, many names. You read many names from the lists that were shown to you and you had something to say about every one of these persons. Also, you said several times that Samac is a small town and that practically everybody knows each other. Because of that, I shall say to you straight away that through my questions, I would like you to clarify some details of this nature which, in my opinion, remained unclear after the direct examination. If you remember some of these things, please answer me. If you don't remember, of course I'm not going to insist. I fully realise that a lot of time has gone by. I would like to start with your invitation to come to the TO to collect weapons. You said that you were phoned by a man whose name you don't remember. I would like to ask you whether you remember how this person introduced himself to you. Did this person say on whose behalf he was calling? Did he introduce himself by his position, first and foremost?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Novak Lukic, Your Honours, I have understood this question. As far as I can remember, I said that this person did not introduce himself, but that person told me to come to the TO staff to take a rifle. However, as far as these lists are concerned, I would like to ask you that we do not lose too much time over this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you anything about lists. This was just an illustration of the point I wish to make.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did go back to the list, and I think it does say in my statement that I do not recall who phoned me. In my statement, I wrote that Salkic Ibrahim, nicknamed Ibela, and many others gave this to me and I did not conceal a thing. As I look at the list that you mentioned to you [as interpreted], the list that I have been looking at for two days, I saw names of my fellow citizens who were registered twice on the same list. And please, in the period from the 17th until the 11th of August, 1992, in Bosanski Samac, no lists were shown to me. The first time I saw lists was here in the courtroom. I would like to ask you to free me of these lists, if possible, because I'm not competent to discuss them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just wait for the questions from counsel, all right? And when he asks a question, you answer just that question. Then we'll move much faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have clarified quite a bit for us by having said what this person said to you, that this person said to you that you should be issued with a weapon; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether this piece of news, that you would get a weapon, frightened you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It upset me and frightened me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you try to refuse this weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not try to refuse to accept this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that this rifle was given to you by Ibrahim Salkic. During the cross-examination by Mr. Zecevic, you said that there were five or six more people there. If I understood you correctly, you were referring to the people who were participating in the distribution of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Over there in the TO premises, did you see Mr. Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You knew him at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: My fellow citizen and friend before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that also before the war, he was a member of your party too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that he was a member of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him at the meetings of your party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this list in the TO premises, the list where you placed your signature upon receipt of the rifle, how many persons were on the list itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of this list. I saw in the yard that there were a large number of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember you said over 100 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that it was primarily Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this group in the yard were there any Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how many, in your estimate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to think about this for a longer period of time, and I would have to have a list of the persons who were present and then I could categorize them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me in approximate percentage terms, I'm not asking for the accurate percentage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an assessment just off the cuff now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But they were primarily Muslims and Croats, that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that the commander of the TO Miloj Bogdanovic was there. The man who worked by him was Janko Dujmusic's son. If you were referring to the Serb ethnicity, they were among the leading people of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have a moment, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that Dujmusic is a Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thinks so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. I never distinguish between people by name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were answering the Prosecutor on the first day, you explained that in the military, you were in the technical service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood you, you spent most of your time working on vehicle maintenance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You -- it's also then that you had been issued with an M-48 rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is an ordinary rifle, not a semi-automatic rifle like the one that was issued to you at the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: After many years, I would see this rifle in my hands as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, you never saw it? You never had it in your hands to be precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, I did not have such weapons in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for these people who gave you this weapon, this rifle, did you tell them that you never had a semi-automatic rifle in your hands before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the possibility to do that, time was very short while this distribution lasted and also the explanation as to how these weapons should be handled and the agreement was that on the 20th of April, on Sunday, 1992, we should meet at the town stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I shall continue along the lines of your last sentence. Do you remember who told you to come to the town stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of these five or six men who were distributing weapons to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said that many people who came there to the TO yard did not get rifles, and that they even protested on account of that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, that day when you got a rifle, you were still a member of the town board of the SDA; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that your party gave a list of names of persons who should be invited to come to the TO to be issued with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a few more questions related to your previous war assignment. Let us clarify these matters in connection with the responses you gave to Mr. Zecevic. [redacted] [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In fact, within that company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we hear what your reserve arms and services were, was it with the JNA or the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your assignment was within your company [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within the TO [redacted], because my company was of military significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, did you ever engage in military exercises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never after 1972 until 1992 I did not have a single military exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You never had a rifle in your hands until the 16th, that is to say, since you got out of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never had a rifle from completing my military service all the way up to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not see Miloj Bogdanovic there, that very place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was mainly Muslims and Croats who got weapons; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days ago during my statement, I said that when I think back, it was mostly Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you thought it was still the old TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That consisted of all the citizens of Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned during your testimony that Aziz Hecimovic came to your house and said you should not go out until a messenger came to get you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that gentleman from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the SDA as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he is one of the founders of the SDA in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of this piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also described the fact that you did take this rifle nevertheless, and you went to the park, to the square in the centre of town at your own initiative, and that over there, you encountered about 15 persons. As far as I remember, you said that they had previously, on the previous day, been at the TO together with you when weapons were being distributed; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your testimony on the 21st, on page 4222, you said that all of them were ethnic Croats and Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now that I go back to that, all of them were Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was not a single armed Serb there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a single armed Serb there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, I'm not clear in my mind which group is now being referred to as "only Croats and Muslims"? Was it the group that gathered in the park or the group that was at the TO collecting weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. We'll have this clarified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have heard what the President said. So which group are we talking about? These 15 people, who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group of 15 people whom I encountered around the centre of my town, on the 17th of April, in the morning, was a group of people from the earlier days when weapons were distributed at the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it now clear enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said you got out spontaneously. Since you spent a couple of hours with these people, do you know whether they had come out spontaneously too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any more. We were all stricken by panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you waiting for someone who was supposed to come there? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous day a larger number of us was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your answer. Let me rephrase my question. You said during your examination-in-chief that you were waiting for a man who was supposed to be in a position of superiority there and you didn't know who this man was. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you can put it that way too. The previous day there were five or six people who were distributing weapons. They too were supposed to come, together with the same number of people who had been in the courtyard of the TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that it was an assembly point where you were supposed to gather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had not been mentioned ever before as an assembly point or otherwise until the 20th of April, when we were supposed to gather at the town stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps the names of any of the people who were there, any of the 15 names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult. It was so many years ago. But I'll try to remember some names. One man's name was Baca. My fellow townsfolk know him well. He was a shepherd. Another man's name was Crvic. He lived in the Lower Mahala. A third man was Hasan. He was the son of the sister of a colleague of mine, Hasan Nurkic -- Galib Nurkic, sorry. Galib Nurkic I really cannot tell you any more names without taking some time off to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't want to go into that much detail. I will just ask you whether Ibrahim Salkic had come there too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Ibrahim Salkic didn't come there. He didn't join that group. I didn't see him until 9.00 p.m. that night, when I heard his voice through the megaphone, without seeing him [as interpreted]. I saw him later at the MUP when I was already detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that later. Thank you. Just another question. You mentioned that one of those men was from Lower Mahala, so not all of the people were from Samac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all from Samac, locals from Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The lower Mahala is a part of Samac, but was everyone from the centre of Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's a part of Samac, it means the person is from Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to another topic. On the 21st of November, in response to one of the Prosecutor's questions, you described how you were forced, in Samac, one night after the 17th of April, to keep your premises in the dark. You were not allowed to turn on lights in your apartments. According to you, that order was not fully observed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our flats were supposed to be dark. Windows were supposed to be covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm interested in. So there was an order to keep flats dark during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber and us what was the meaning and what was the purpose of this, of keeping your windows and flats in darkness? I mean, as you see it, I would like to know how you understand it, why you were supposed to cover your windows with blankets and not turn your lights on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know. Probably because of the aviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the purpose of keeping premises dark was to rule out the possibility of damage from night-time shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know was that I behaved as a conscientious citizen. I obeyed and complied with every order and instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. I'll ask you another question. Would a well-lit house be a better target for shelling at night than one which is not lit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you mentioned your meeting with Ibela, Ibela. I would like just one more clarification. Specifically, the shooting in Samac - and I think this has become undisputed here - was heard, was audible, between the 16th and 17th of April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have already established that it was during the night between Thursday and Friday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was imprinted on my memory, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you said that you heard Ibela speaking through a megaphone, saying that weapons should be left outside houses at 9.00 on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you complied with that order and turned over your rifle -- that is, your wife turned over your rifle to a young man, and as you put it yourself, you were in possession of that rifle between 1600 and 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't wait to get rid of it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. I was in possession of the rifle for 16 or 17 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you had the rifle for less than one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just given you the correct number of hours as I calculated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you turned over the rifle after you heard Ibela's instructions through the megaphone to turn over the weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear sir, since I heard shooting, fire exchanges, from the earliest hours of that day, and I saw houses and the school building burning, I could hardly wait to give this rifle to someone, so I turned it over to this young man. And I was waiting for some reasonable force to come to Samac and tell people, "You've had enough of this suffering and uncertainty," and to introduce some order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you complied with that order after you heard Ibela speaking through a megaphone. That's what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like you to answer a couple of questions regarding your stay in Batkovici and your exchange. You were transferred to Batkovici on the 27th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also stated that on the 13th of December, the same year, you were registered by the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were taken to the military court in Bijeljina for the first time in end December of the same year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it was sometime in spring 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any decision from the court before the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of decision do you mean? I don't understand your question, Mr. Novak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a decision ruling your remand in custody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: After six or seven months in detention, I was told that I had been convicted and there was also a decision that I was supposed to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before you were transferred to Bijeljina, had you given any statements to any official authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a procedure. Everybody was supposed to give a statement in the admissions office, and in the course of the first seven days I, too, gave a statement to the investigations judge in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was in August, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was during the first days of my detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that Miroslav Tadic was in Batkovici for the last time in June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the exchange of my fellow townsfolk in the month of August -- in the month of June it was they were exchanged, and what I stated was that I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was Ibrahim Salkic together with you at the camp in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a while, and he was taken to Vlasenica for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How about Omer Nalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was with me in the camp and for a while, he was taken to Vlasenica as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was Pasaga Tihic together with you in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. As far as I know, he was taken away to Vlasenica for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you share a hangar with any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken to Vlasenica and when he got back there after the exchange, we were together in the same hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that these people were exchanged in that last exchange in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never went together, all of us, only a group would be taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But after July 1993, they were no longer in Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need some time to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have just said that before the exchange, they were in the same hangar with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before one of the exchanges, there were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to tender two lists for exchanges dating back to June 1993. These lists have been translated by official authorised translators into English so we have a complete set of evidence. I would like to introduce first one list and then the other, and then I would like to ask this witness a couple of questions regarding the lists. They were delivered to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of September in the process of reciprocal disclosure, and they have had them since then and also all of these have been made available to the translation unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to the interpreters, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the numbers, please? First of all, I want to find out from the Prosecution ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm just looking at them now, if Your Honours please. I don't think there will be a problem. May I just have a moment to look at them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can see no reason to object to the admission of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D13/3 ter, and D13/3 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose, Witness, that you haven't seen this before, but I would just like you to read the title, the heading, that is, and the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1st Krajina Corps Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War, Banja Luka, date, 1st of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please slow down please this has to be interpreted. To whom is this addressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska to the commission, attention Colonel Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is written below that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you don't mind, please read the sentence which is marked in yellow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We have succeeded in reaching an agreement with the representatives of the HVO of Posavina about the exchange of prisoners from the area of Orasje the prison of Lower Mahala. Please approve the proposed package, because the exchange will take place on Saturday, the 5th of June 1993 in Dragalic on the highway."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, do you see on this list the names of your fellow citizens that I asked you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, sir, a lot of my fellow citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean the three we have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among ordinary townsfolk, I see the three that we have mentioned recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you would be so kind as to read the last sentence on page 2 which is also highlighted and the name of the person who is the author of this letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The commission of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska is kindly requested to issue, upon approval, an order to the prisons in Batkovici, Doboj and Banja Luka on the separation of prisoners, selection of prisoners for exchange to be conducted by the commission of the 1st Krajina Corps Banja Luka." And it is signed as President Milutin Grujicic, Captain First Class.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the stamp is visible enough, can you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military post code, Banja Luka. The Cyrillic script is something that I am very familiar with because I learned it in primary school. However, I notice very much that both scripts are often used in the same letter but I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't mind either. Have you heard about Milutin Grujicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to tender my second document dealing with the same exchange. It's of the same nature, but addressed to a different institution. It is accompanied by an official translation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, looking at this document and the official translation, I get the impression that this was a list prepared "yet to be approved," not that this is -- these were actually exchanged from the evidence of this document. My understanding is that this list was prepared, it was yet to be approved for purposes of exchange. That's your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. position? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is completely correct. I want to prove who makes decisions, who gives approval, and what the procedure is in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Judge Williams has a question too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in looking at these lists, I think this is the first time we've had mention of prisoners of war. So is my understanding correct that these lists were for the exchange of combatant prisoners of war as opposed to civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right, Your Honour. This commission, which is officially called "The Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War from Banja Luka," attached to the 1st Krajina Corps, which was part of the army of Republika Srpska, decided on exchanges of persons which they claimed had the status of prisoners of war, in view of proceedings that had taken place before military courts. All prisoners in Batkovici were exchanged through military commissions, with military commissions of the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one sort of thought I have therefor, and I presume we'll be hearing, as the trial progresses, evidence on this. Obviously, the treatment of prisoners of war is governed by the Geneva Conventions 1949 and the two additional protocols to those conventions of 1977, and as I'm sure we're all aware, one of the provisions concerns treatment of prisoners of war and the rights of a fair and regular trial and also the right not to be subjected to beatings, and so on and so forth. I'm not asking a question on that; I'm just sort of putting it out as something that I'm sure will need to be addressed at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. The Defence has planned this since the beginning of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And in addition to that -- because we've heard evidence of how some of the people who were not combatants but were detained, treated the way the evidence has gone so far, and then later on charged and tried and sentenced, so there seems to be additional parts, and whether all that is included in the claim of them being prisoners of war, that is another -- just a detail which I wanted to have clarified later on in the trial, and especially during the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic. Just one last question here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And this is a question for the witness. In looking at the list, Witness, the three highlighted names - number 7, 10, and 11 - did you know these three people to be military people, to be combatants, or civilians? Could you give us your opinion on that, or your knowledge rather than your opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These people are my fellow citizens who had worked in enterprises. They were by no means military men. I don't know whether they were in possession of any weapons on the 17th of April. All of these people are my fellow citizens who were civilians, who were employed in various enterprises until the 17th of April, 1992. And I also know that Esef Zaimbegovic was director of Uniglas; Arminko Puric; Husein Arapovic; Mirsad Gebic, and some others. There are people whom I don't know, and they must -- they are probably from the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch all the last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will only add one minor clarification. On page 2 of this list, we have a list of 21 persons, and these are persons offered for exchange by the other side. And we can see by their place of residence that they are Serbs, but I can also put it in the form of question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting, but I just want to be clear about the evidence. Which document is my learned friend referring to? I assume we're still on D13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: /3, yes. Yes, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because page 2 also starts from number 1, up to 21. Yes, Counsel. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a question to the witness. Can he give his opinion concerning the persons on page 2? According to their names and surnames and their place of birth, are they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many last names are well known to me, my fellow citizens who came to the town of Samac, and many of them probably lived in the town of Samac. However, in terms of the place where they were born, I see that they were outside Samac. Most probably, many of them worked in Bosanski Samac as well, in work organisations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My only question was whether they were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never distinguished people by their names and surnames. I don't know how they would declare themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you testified, when you spoke about the ethnic composition of arrested persons, when you spoke of the ethnic composition of the persons assembled in the square, when you spoke of the ethnic composition of persons who were waiting in line for permits to leave Samac, then you did know the ethnic background of these people. I'm putting a simple question to you. These surnames and names and places of birth, do they indicate to you what the ethnic background of these persons is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I would say that they were all of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just one or two clarifications, Witness. On which side of the border is the prison Donja Mahala? Is it on the Bosnia-Herzegovinian side or on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you meant a particular locality in my town of Samac, that is practically the centre of the town of Bosanski Samac. The locality itself was called Donja Mahala, and there was Gornja Mahala, Bosnari, Savari, but all of that is an integral part of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And where exactly is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Singh, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Where exactly is Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Batkovici is not far away from Bijeljina, where the Drina flows into the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So that's still in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. Lukic, this is a clarification from you. You had tried to describe this document D13/3, and you said that, in amplification, the proceedings had taken place before a military tribunal. Is that correct or was it a civilian court where the present witness was charged and convicted?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in about ten minutes I shall move on to the topic of his trial, and I believe that the documents will show quite clearly where he was tried and on the basis of which documents. To the best of our knowledge, this witness was tried before the court in Bijeljina and the Supreme Military Court of Republika Srpska. However, we shall be discussing this with the witness quite soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But since you know, can you tell us, was it a military tribunal or was it a civilian court that they were tried in?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, a military court. Exclusively a military court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In response to Judge Singh's question, I would like to seek some clarification. The area of Orasje, who had authority over the area of Orasje during the war, military authority, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, during the war, I was never in Orasje. People said that it was the HVO that was in power there, the Croat Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there is a place called Donja Mahala in the municipality of Orasje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a place called Donja Mahala in the municipality of Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only wish to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the second list, I don't know whether we have received a number for it from the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We haven't yet seen it. I take it it's the same position with this one from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's been properly translated and it was disclosed to us, so there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D14/3 ter, and D14/3 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask you that we move through this document in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you read the letterhead, please, everything that was highlighted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps. It's to the Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War, Banja Luka, the 3rd of June, 1993, to the Eastern Bosnia Corps, to Colonel Pero Koljevic, Bijeljina. "We kindly ask Colonel Pero Koljevic to help us in organising the package of exchanges with the representatives of the HVO Posavina, Orasje. We have agreed on this, and approval should arrive any moment, and we kindly ask you personally to help us in separating prisoners from Batkovici. The group of prisoners envisaged for an exchange will be taken over by a member of the mixed commission from Samac, Miro Tadic, who will, at the same time, contact you. We look forward to your help and we thank you." We have envisaged the following prisoners, Croats and Muslims, from Batkovici to be exchanged."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please just look at the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chairman Milutin Grujicic, Captain First Class.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this list, we see again these three persons that I asked you about at the beginning; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the list, we see -- from the first, 20, and here there are 21. So for one, no agreement was reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also see that the date here is two days after the first date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 3rd and the 1st, you're right, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the prison of Donja Mahala that was in the territory of the municipality of Orasje and under the control of the Croat Defence Council there were Serbs who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, during the war I was never in the territory of Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just asked you whether you were aware of this fact, not whether you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us at the hangar knew that regardless of whether people were brought from their homes or whether these were combatants brought in from the front line, we all knew the other side should have the same number of Serbs in order for an exchange to be carried out. Where they were detained, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you ask the question, I just want clarification. The witness looked at this list, D14/3, you asked him that there are three names which were discussed in the other list, in D13/3, there were three names discussed and then in this list, D14/3, the same three names do appear. Are these the names at 7, 10, and 11 for clarification? That's all. That is the correct -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to put another question to you now related to the previous one. You were detained in August 1992 and until then, you did what you described to my colleague, Mr. Zecevic, and to the Prosecutor. Do you know what happened on the 8th of May in Odzak, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the war, I was never in the territory of Odzak until the 17th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we haven't understood each other again. I just asked you whether you knew what happened in Odzak on that day, if you do know, if you heard about it tell us about it. If you don't know, you don't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 8th of May, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that all Serbs who lived in the territory of the municipality of Odzak were detained in the month of May 1992 by the Croat Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the opportunity of hearing over Radio Serb Samac already in the beginning of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you heard about this piece of news?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about it over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into private session now, Your Honours, because I would like to put a few questions related to the trial before the military court in Bijeljina. Also on this occasion, I would like to tender some documents related to these proceedings; however, regrettably, I have not got any official translations of these documents yet although I did ask the registrar for it. So I would like to analyse this with the witness. These are two decisions and one judgement. I have no note that these documents were submitted to us by the Prosecution and, according to the letter that we got from the OTP, it seems that this witness personally had submitted these documents to the OTP; however, we are going to clarify this clue through our questions. I would kindly ask the usher for his assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So then the documents discussed during private session will be under seal, just to make sure that the particulars and the names are not revealed, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said, on the 22nd November, in response to a question by Mr. Zecevic, that you were not a member of the military wing of the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the war, were you a member of a group of the so-called Self-Organised Citizens of Bosanski Samac for the defence of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that members of this group formed patrols which patrolled the town, armed patrols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I said I was a member, it means as soon as I got one, on the 16th, it means I belonged with them. It means that my fellow citizens from the reserve police force patrolled a part of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that these people were exclusively members of the reserve police force who patrolled this town, or were there other citizens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the line of examination, but it's not -- the evidence is not clear to me, and particularly what the witness is saying. Is he referring to the TO or some other organisation, something called the Self-Organised Citizens of Bosanski Samac? Is that the same as the TO or not? And the Chamber would be well served to know exactly what the witness is talking about when he claims membership of this body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Yes. Can we have clarification by you, Counsel, through the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can tell you exactly what I meant. I meant the 16th of April, 1992, when I received a weapon from the TO, I immediately joined the organised defence of Bosanski Samac, became a member of that defence. The patrols that existed earlier, during daytime and night-time, came from the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I have just asked you: Were you aware of the fact that there existed a group of self-organised citizens of Bosanski Samac whose members were included in the patrols without being members of the reserve police force or the police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that your own party, of which you were a member, drew up a list of your own members who, before the 16th of April, 1992, patrolled the streets of the town of Samac as party members of these patrols representing the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, only police reservists were in these patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So to conclude, you don't know that your party organised any kind of patrols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you have explained, you were arrested on the 27th of August, 1992 and you were exchanged on the 4th of October, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what I said was the 11th of August, 1992, and as far as the exchange is concerned, it was on the 4th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Now I would like to ask you a couple of questions about the exchange itself. I think you have already mentioned this, and I'm sorry about the repetition, but tell us again: How many of you from Batkovici went to be exchanged to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Sometimes it was a smaller group, sometimes it was a larger group. I think we were about 20. I think that included 12 of us locals who were taken to the Serbian Sarajevo and over the separation line, across the separation line. That's where we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you taken to be exchanged by uniformed persons? The people who took you to be exchanged, did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone but the prisoners wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the place, at the venue of the exchange itself, were there officers present from both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the venue itself, in Serbian Sarajevo, there were Serbian soldiers and the command. I was transferred by an UNPROFOR transporter for 500 metres in the direction of Sarajevo, which was controlled by the BH army. There I found some people in civilian clothing and some people in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us specify. You found some people dressed in BH army uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Amo Masovic and his deputy Odobasic. They participated personally in the exchange. They did not have camouflage uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, who is Amor Masovic; what was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was chairman of the commission for exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said you were transferred by an UNPROFOR vehicle. Were there any other international humanitarian organisations represented such as the ICRC, the European community, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very procedure of my transfer from Batkovici and the exchange lasted about 20 hours. In those 20 hours, I was brought to a prison called Kula which was controlled by the Serb side. As far as I remember, that's how they introduced themselves as representatives of the International Red Cross. At that time, I had contact with them, but I don't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, as you mentioned to the Prosecutor, they asked you whether you wanted to go to the other side. Did these representatives ask you that, and where did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the many questions that was addressed to me was that question as well. This was in the prison in Kula in the Serb Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that at the moment when you were transferred, when the exchange was carried out, you had had about half of your prison sentence left, the five-year prison sentence that you read about a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this rigged prison sentence, about half of it was left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only a few more questions, but I think we should move into private session again because of a few documents that I would like to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, before I put the first question to you, I would like to say, on behalf of my client, that he is very sorry about all the bad things that happened to you and all the suffering you experienced. I would like to clarify certain details in relation to an incident that occurred with regard to your [redacted]house [redacted]. You have already explained to us that you had engaged a certain [redacted], and you said, if I remember correctly, that since you were not 100 per cent sure that you would get the right kind of information from him for the money that you had been giving him, that you took your wife along, as well as Sulejman Tihic, in order to attend this meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you received information from him to the effect that this was done by Fadil Topcagic and Igor Rukavina, if I have understood your statement correctly that that is what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what was said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am only interested in one detail now. This Igor Rukavina, I need to identify him, because you mention him in your statement. Is that the same person that the Serb forces arrested when you were at the meeting in the yard of the factory Buducnost and accused him of being a sniper shooter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you know, can you tell me: Is he a Croat by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he is. His father is an ethnic Croat and his mother is a Muslim. What he declared himself to be, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question with regard to this topic. In relation to this incident, were criminal charges brought against any of the perpetrators, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with my [redacted] house?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited. [redacted] was registered as a private detective, and he told me that I should wait for him officially to make a submission to the MUP in Bosanski Samac, that he should submit a report to them. That was the agreement that he and I had had.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I understand your answer correctly, it means that this report was not filed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move on to another subject, briefly. In your statement, you mentioned that as for the existence of the 4th Detachment, you heard about that towards the end of 1991. We had several witnesses here, and we have also heard other information. Can you perhaps allow for the possibility that this happened in the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I was not sufficiently informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that this perhaps happened at the beginning of 1992 rather than at the end of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot allow for that possibility [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move on to another subject, and that is the [redacted], the day when you were arrested. You said to us that these persons who arrested you at your house were a certain Milan from Crkvina, and you also said that together with him was another man who worked at the department store selling wall-to-wall carpeting but that you could not remember his name. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This person, this second person, this other person, not Milan, but this other person, was that perhaps a person whose nickname was Zvaka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Later on, at the SUP, I met Zvaka, but that was not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these two persons, when they arrested you, they took you to the SUP; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By way of clarification, we understand this, but that is the police station, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that, did you see any more of these two men who arrested you and brought you to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: This gentleman who, to the best of my knowledge, worked as a salesperson selling wall-to-wall carpeting at the department store is a member of the police of Republika Srpska until the present day, and he is working in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is precisely one of the things that I wished to clarify. They took you to the SUP, to the reception office at the SUP, at the police station; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, then, that these two men were members of the police, these two men who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 17th of April, I believe they were members of the police. Until the 17th, they were not members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At the moment when you were being arrested, or after that, while you were detained at the police station, did they ever tell you on whose orders they arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was getting dressed, they said on whose orders they were doing this. They said this to my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on whose orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this perhaps on the orders of the then chief of police of the SUP, Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you said that unfortunately you saw Stevan Todorovic often there, accompanied by five or six more persons. Can you tell me if you recall what kind of a uniform Stevan Todorovic had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times, he wore a black camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these five or six persons who were accompanying Stevan Todorovic, were they policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what kind of uniforms did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there any difference between the uniforms of the Serb police and military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this difference was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb police wore blue uniforms. The Serb military wore camouflage suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So to the best of your knowledge, the difference was in colour, one wore green and the other wore blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there Serb policemen who wore green camouflage uniforms; do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, we have got some information about this, but you can confirm it for us. Was Stevan Todorovic chief of police, the head of the SUP as it was called then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, there was a gentleman called Stoko. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you a very specific question: Was he head of the SUP? But then I can ask you do you know who the commander of the station was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not really go into their powers. For me, they were all citizens of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. I am not going to insist. If you don't know, you don't know. Now, I would like to put a small number of questions to you pertaining to Odzak when you went there to work. You already said to us that this was the day when the mosque exploded and you said just before that explosion you were informed about this and that you saw sought shelter in a basement in a building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, were Dzevad Celic and Zlatko Tiric with you on work duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm asking about the two of them, yes. And when you got into that shelter there were a lot of people in that shelter, perhaps about 100 persons in that shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went down into that shelter, there wasn't anyone there. After that us, four men appeared, the four men I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any women, perhaps, in the shelter where you were down there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four women who also came from my town, the town of Bosanski Samac who were brought with me together in the same group.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreter said they didn't understand the last part of the answer. Can the witness repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That were four women with me and they were brought there to work together with us men in order to clean up the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just have one more question for you. In your statement, you described in detail, if I can put it that way, what Odzak looked like the moment when you arrived. There were soldiers all over the place, the tractors were coming in, some people were being brought in, others were going out. Do you know about the population of Odzak, the civilians who lived in Odzak before this happened? Had they left town with the military? Was this an abandoned town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, two or three days earlier, they left the town of Odzak. They withdrew in the direction of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions. I told you it was going to be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, you commented in answer to Mr. Zecevic's questions that you had an occasion to see Mr. Milan Simic's office and that it was nicely decorated. When did you have that opportunity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime in July 1992 when I was loading sand into sacks near the memorial house and we dragged the property of Hurtic on little trolleys in the direction of the memorial house, and we were placing those sandbags on the lower floor of the municipal assembly, placing them on the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you just look inside or were you, for some reason, taken into the office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken, several of us, into the office because we were assigned the task of taking sandbags from people who were giving them to us from outside to make it easier, and I was one of those people, one of those men, who were on the inside of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Milan Simic present when you went inside the office taking sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw Milan Simic again after he issued me with that certificate which was on the fifth or the sixth day of war. I never saw him again in that office. I did find there, however, many of my townsfolk who ordered us how to go about our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How can you say that the office belonged to Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that from those people that it was Milan Simic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Approximately how far from the SUP and the TO was the office distance-wise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the SUP, this office which was in the building of the municipal assembly, and it was actually another wing of the same building about 10 to 15 metres, as the crow flies, across the street or across the yard, there was the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you were asked questions, I believe, as to whether or not the sandbags would affect sound coming into the room or into the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked questions about that. I'm not a great expert. I think that sandbags were placed as protection from shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Prior to your placing the sandbags there, that is, before you started the job, was the building free of sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first time, we were given the task to place those sandbags, and there had been none on the windows, as far as I could ascertain visually. We placed the first bags, and we continued placing more sandbags, and more people came the next day to do the same job.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zecevic asked you some questions about a document, D23/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could the witness please briefly be shown that document. And may I see the document itself, Mr. Usher, before it's presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just one very brief question about that document, Witness. You were asked by Mr. Zecevic if the signature of Sejdinovic was there on that document and you said yes, and you can see, indeed, at the bottom right-hand portion of the document the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What I want to know is this: Can you tell us if that is the name of Sejdinovic written out in handwriting or whether that is his signature? Do you understand the difference and, if so, tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. It is not typed here, it is handwritten. I had no working contacts with him since primary school so I don't know whether it is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were asked questions by Mr. Zecevic, I think, touching upon the role of Milan Simic and another gentleman named Jovanovic at the Uniglas factory when you went to get your note permitting you passage past the checkpoints. Is there anything that you saw or observed on that occasion that indicated to you hierarchy between those two gentlemen, namely, anything that you saw or observed that made you think that Milan Simic was Jovanovic's superior, or vice versa? And if you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't conclude anything about that, but it was Milan Simic who signed the paper for me, and that paper allowed me to move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions, both by Defence counsel, Mr. Zecevic, and by the Chamber as well, by the Judges, regarding the rent, the possible collection of rent held on your behalf, if indeed that has ever occurred, at the municipality. Have you ever been told or informed in any way at all prior to coming here to give evidence, prior to coming to The Hague to give evidence, that rents were ever collected and held on your behalf in Bosanski Samac? [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never informed. In contacts I had with my fellow citizens, I never got information to the effect that anyone was paid, either myself or the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Not only information that you were paid, but I'm also extending my question to this: Have you ever been told or informed that rents were paid and that they were held on your behalf at the municipality, in trust, so to speak? That's what I want to know: Has anyone ever told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I will want to put some of the documents that were put to you this morning now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And for the purposes -- for the assistance of the usher, the two that I want to refer to now are D13/3 and D14. I dare say, it would be wise to have both the English and the original. Can we start, please, with D14. I do apologise. Can we start, please, with D13.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this document says that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There's a reference in this document to prisoners of war, and I want you to look at the names of the people listed there. Do you know any of them? And I'm referring to the first page, where there are 21 numbers with names next to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know many of my fellow citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about Ivo Lucic [phoen]? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about the next one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Just run your finger down the list slowly until you come to a man who you do know, and I'll ask you about that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was his occupation in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in the electrical company until the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he involved in any fighting prior to the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no fighting before the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about the next one? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esref Zaimbegovic, my fellow citizen. He was the manager, the director of the Uniglas company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he involved or a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't belong to any military formation, ever, not even on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What background is he? Ethnic background, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just tell the Chamber quickly - read them out - which of those men, continuing on from Esref Zaimbegovic and running your finger down the list, which of them are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be quicker if you can tell us if any of them aren't Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names I've read so far, all of them, to the best of my knowledge, are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Anyone there at all that you see on that list, anyone at all, that you know was engaged in fighting or a member of any sort of military unit prior to April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, for all of these fellow citizens I've mentioned, I can say with certainty that they were not armed prior to the 16th of April and they were not members, because they had work obligation in the companies with which they were employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if any of them are old men, or were old men back then? By that subjective question -- but let's start at, say, 60 onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted it specify the age.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's start from about 60 onwards, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this list, I don't see anyone who is older, that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
