utterances.text: Thank you. Turn over the page, and there's a list there of 21 names, and I think Defence counsel suggested to you that they might be people of Serbian ethnic background. Do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of the surnames are familiar, but I've lost contact with my fellow citizens to a large extent. So there may be many citizens on this list who worked, coming to my town on bicycles and by car to perform their work duty, but I cannot remember with any certainty which of the people here were the ones. But that is easy to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've done with those two documents. Can the witness be shown documents that were produced to him this morning, D17, D15, D16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do any of them contain particulars of the witness, Mr. di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour, they do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It would be wise to go into private session. Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Witness L, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now finished. We are now finished with your evidence. You are free to go. But just wait for the usher to take you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In the absence of Mr. Simic, which had been indicated in the morning that he was not well today and he wouldn't come, so we are not able to start with a new witness in his absence. I just wanted to find out from the Defence. There is an indication that they are not ready to make submissions after the documents regarding Variant A and B were submitted to them, were given to them by the Prosecution, and I just want to say if they can be ready with that as from tomorrow, depending on what situation will unfold, we might -- I might ask for their submissions, final submissions, so that the Trial Chamber can make a ruling on that. I wonder whether there are any other matters that counsel wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think my colleagues have something, but just in addition to the first issue, Madam President, just to inform you. It's just a technical matter. We didn't get the materials with us because we didn't obtain any information that we have to discuss this. It's a situation that is beyond our knowledge that -- with all these technical issues this afternoon. So as of tomorrow we shall be ready to proceed with this issue. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you -- if this Trial Chamber pleases, there are two, actually, things I would like to raise. One thing is a short clarification, because I was invited by this Honourable Trial Chamber on Thursday to give an explanation about the law on abandoned property. If you remember when I was cross-examining the witness, there was a certain part which I explained. And I used my time over the weekend to really clarify this position, and I wouldn't like to bring this Honourable Trial Chamber -- or that this Honourable Trial Chamber understands that I was misleading the Trial Chamber or my colleagues or the witnesses. That is why I would like to give a very short clarification on that. And then after that I have one motion which I have to say before this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Present.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Present, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you can go ahead with your first point on abandoned property.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, if you remember, the matter was raised about the law on abandoned property, and I have, as I said, I have used my time over the weekend and found out that this law was actually passed in February 1996 in Official Gazette number 3, and it was published in Official Gazette of Republika Srpska number 3 of February 27th, 1996. The amendments --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that is the current law as of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the current law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because this is 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 1996. There were amendments to this law in Official Gazette number 29 of 1996 and 38 of 1998. So this -- actually, the text of the original law has been amended to some extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Twice, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the principle is just the same. Actually, in accordance with the law, the municipalities were obliged to submit the list of abandoned property --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, before you proceed, when you say "in accordance with the law," this 1996 one or previous --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As of 1996, the situation was as you are trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours. According to this law of February 1996, which is named Law on Abandoned Property, the municipalities throughout Republika Srpska were obliged to submit the lists of the abandoned property to the government of Republika Srpska, or rather, to the Ministry for the Refugees of the Government of Republika Srpska. So in case -- this property, according to the law, means houses, land, business space, as well as cars, furniture, and practically everything which is property. In case of business space, the ministry have established a public enterprise of Republika Srpska for management and administration of business premises. This particular enterprise, which is a governmentally owned enterprise and it is founded under the auspices of the government, is actually managing these business spaces throughout Republika Srpska, including Bosanski Samac. What was in practice done was that certain individuals, or the third parties who liked to rent a certain business space, approached this enterprise of -- which I said was governmentally owned and is under auspices of the government, and signed a contract with this enterprise. And this enterprise was entitled to receive the monthly rent for the usage of this business space. The point is that this is different from what I said on Thursday was that I believe that at that time, it was the municipal authorities that were collecting the rent, but actually when I got deeper into this, I found out that this is really a government enterprise which was really managing and administrating all these business premises. That was the actually clarification which I like to make and, of course, I wish to apologise for this incorrectness but really, Your Honours, at that time, I really thought -- because I misinterpreted this provision of the law that the municipality was obliged to do the lists and I thought consequently or by analogy, the municipality was doing it the rest of the contracts and the rent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for the correction. Before you go to the other motion, in case there are questions for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So actually thank you for your clarification, Mr. Zecevic. So this question of abandoned property doesn't feature in this case then?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: The question of the abandoned property does not arise in this particular case. It is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's very relevant, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: What was the abandoned property that is relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the abandoned property is the business property throughout Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: No, in this particular case, concerning this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Witness K had the abandoned property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You've heard his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You've heard his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: The boutique was given to someone, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the usage, yes, on the basis of this contract, but it was in accordance with the law of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But that law came into force in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But in this particular case, it had been given for usage before 1996. So the contractual obligations would apply rather than the statutory obligations under an abandonment, and if it is relevant, you have put none of these facts to the witness concerning abandonment, concerning going to the municipality, telling the municipality that so and so would like to use this property, and I will pay rent. These things should have been put.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honours, that I did put to the witness during my cross-examination the -- if you remember, Your Honour, I was really going into the matter whether his ownership was disputed at any time since April 17th until the moment when -- in the year 2000 he regained the possession of his property. And that is actually, in my mind, the most significant part of -- I mean the most significant issue in this. Also, if I may remind you, Your Honour, the -- my learned colleague, Mr. Prosecutor, had asked the witness: Whom did you find in your [redacted] when you came back to Bosanski Samac? And then he said it was a sister of my client, and that has happened in 1999. And therefore, it is relevant and it is -- I mean this law was already in place at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in 1998, I believe, but it was during the time when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- after the law was initiated. That was the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mm-hm. Okay. And Judge Williams would like to ask also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering, is the legislation simply prospective in terms of giving compensation to those persons who own the property but were dispossessed because they were in camps and so on and so forth or is it also retroactive dating to the point in time when the person would have been detained and taken from Bosanski Samac for example?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, as this law was concerned, this law was actually done on the basis of the Dayton Accord, and obviously the provisions of the Dayton Accord do have implication on this particular law as well as all the contracts which are signed between this enterprise and the third parties who were using. Because in the contract, there is a certain article which says that in case the legitimate owner requests his -- to regain the possession of his property, this contract on usage becomes null and void in accordance with the Dayton Accord. That is one aspect. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The other aspect of this law, it doesn't really, in this particular law, it doesn't say that everybody is entitled to compensation for whatever reasons, but it is my understanding that in other laws this subject was really principled subjects that they were dealing with. But only in this law it says that at the time when this law was passed or brought to life, so to speak, back in 1996, anyone who was using the space, so-called abandoned space, the business space, anybody who was using the space without the title was to leave immediately and would be taken out of these premises by force, and the owner is entitled to compensation and damages for the usage of this until 1996. So that is -- I mean in that respect, this law really goes into the matter you were asking me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one small point after that. You are mentioning business space, so what about residential housing space?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this particular -- this particular law goes on -- I mean goes for all -- and the provisions which I was talking about goes on all the property; houses, land, and all that. Only for the business space, this enterprise was formed because the business space was rented out. The rest of it, I don't think it was rented out at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Your case, Mr. Zecevic, is that the sister was paying rent to the municipality and this witness's family can collect the rent from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it is my understanding that if this witness would ask the -- in the proper legal way the government of Republika Srpska that he be repaid, remunerated for the rent during the time while the rent was paid by the sister of my -- or any other tenant, I believe he is entitled to gain this amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course -- if I may, of course, with a little help of lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You can always assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me summarise one thing. I mean we are going beyond certain -- we didn't intervene during the examination-in-chief about these particular issues. Firstly, we have a timeframe of our indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what is the relevance to ask witness about his property in 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, and 1999. We understand the position of the witness. They are entitled to present their situation and so on, but simply, you know, to the normal level. This is nothing without our indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I quite understand your point, but sometimes for the witness's sake, it is better that the problem is completed as far as he understands it, even if it goes beyond the period of the indictment. It's just for completeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I very well aware why the witness should be heard here, not only about certain facts but still because of all these tragic events. But still, we are professionals. So let me summarise the issues. During the wartime, according to my knowledge, in Republika Srpska was -- the government of Republika Srpska adopted a decree on the governmental level which is actually the same which is the law adopted in 1996 that my colleague speaks. So the Defence will be very happy to, during our case and, of course, maybe during cross-examination, to inform this Trial Chamber about this set of laws and also let me also inform you that we are collecting the extracts from the court records of the properties, from the registry of the properties of all these witnesses and they are -- they names are through all these wartime listed. Nobody depossessed [sic] them from the official court register. They were, in fact, depossessed due to the fact that they left the area. That's another story. But specifically speaking about the property, that's another thing, and we have here all these witnesses they are not professionals, so they don't know to whom they should address, where they have recollect their money or try to assistance. So to some extent it seems that we are losing the control over the issues that we have discussed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. You see, Mr. Pantelic, the point is when a witness describes how he was ill-treated, what he has lost, it simply ends there. The consequence of not completing, if at all anything mitigates that loss, is that the sentencing aspect, should we come to that, should there be a conviction, will take into account the loss of the property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So even if it goes beyond the indictment period to explain -- for a witness to explain that, "This is what has happened. I've now got my house back," I've now got whatever, it helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely it helps. But if Defence were in situation to present certain facts with respect to the financial amount of money collected through the government on behalf of the depossessed persons, maybe that would be another angle of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because it would go to, perhaps, the mitigating. But to show that for a period of time they were dispossessed for the criminal activities, we are limited, but to show that there has been an improvement in the status of the witness who may be considered a victim, it may help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the higher level, because we are speaking about the governmental level. You know, local authorities don't have anything with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Whatever it is, as long as the victim or the witness, who is a victim, has got an improved situation, regardless of which authority makes that possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the bottom line is that there are legal possibilities and remedies that all of them will be remunerated for this period of time. So I mean, this is the situation absolutely now in Republika Srpska, as well as in Federation, Muslim Croat Federation, which was the same. Not in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is beside the point. Yes, Mr. Zecevic, you wanted to put up a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Your Honours, yesterday we received material by the Prosecutor about the new coming witness, Witness K, and this summary which was given to us contains new information which are not contained in the statement of the witness, in the previous statement which we were given. A lot of this information is not relevant to the allegations in the indictment, and therefore we are making an oral motion in limine as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me first express my thoughts to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution has given you information. This is after proofing, do I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, you are the one dealing with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Phillip Weiner for the OTP. Yes. As a matter of background, Your Honour, about three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, there was some discussion - I believe Mr. -- Attorney Pantelic raised the issue - of new matters being raised for the first time during direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examination-in-chief, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As a result, for the last two witnesses -- last two or three that we have handled, what we have done is when we have proofed witnesses and gone over any new matters that have arisen, we have turned it over. For Mr. Esad Dagovic, I gave them a three- or four-page letter indicating all of the new information, which I think is fair and just. I don't know if it's -- I don't believe it's required by the Rules; however, it is the fair and just thing to do. That's what -- I know I would do this in the United States with my own cases. We did this again involving this case here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness K, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What we did do with relation to many of these issues is we talked about the witnesses and we brought out more detail. The specific allegations relating to Milan Simic which he's related to, which are allegation of sexual assault, were described in the initial police reports that have been provided. We have now given him some additional detail related to those assaults, but those are the issues which he's dealing with. I think he wants to file some sort of motion in limine at this point. But I just want to say that we've done the fair thing and the right thing by filing discovery, which is not required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. First of all, it is not a matter of sexual assault and has never been a matter of sexual assault. It is extramarital affairs which were alleged in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's extra what? I can't understand. Extramarital?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Extramarital affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, extramarital affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, and not the sexual assault. The point is, Your Honours, we have -- we are losing so much time during this examination-in-chief of the witnesses to the things which are not relevant and not in the indictment, such as this. If there was an indication of the sexual assault or whatever, I would assume that the Prosecutor would indict or charge our client with this kind of behaviour, but he has not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but if the Prosecution is going to lead irrelevant evidence, of course it will be -- it will not be allowed by the Trial Chamber and it may be objected to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but actually, we are trying to save time for this Trial Chamber, and for us as well, that we make this motion in limine before, so we don't get into these objections and rulings of the Trial Chamber during the actual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- examination-in-chief of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what particulars are you objecting to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we are objecting to three particulars. First of all, we think that the Prosecution and witness should be prevented from going into these particulars. First particular is that we and the OTP have stipulated that our client, Mr. Milan Simic, has been appointed to the post of president of the Executive Board from May 30th, 1992. So everything which has any -- everything which goes before that period is not relevant, in our opinion. On the other hand, any evidence suggesting and regarding these extramarital affairs are not relevant to the allegations in the indictment or are not a crime, and in our mind, they are, first, not relevant, and are prejudicial to our defendant. The third thing which also is in the summary: Any evidence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. regarding defendants making exchanges or bribes to make exchanges are not alleged in the indictment, and the defendant was not charged about that. He was not charged under the Article 2. So these are the allegations which appeared just in this summary this morning, and we would like to make this motion in limine that we don't have to go -- to object all the time during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because you consider them as not part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. No. I do not consider them; it is a fact that they are not part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, unless it's very, very brief, we are going beyond the time. Especially the interpreters are being detained unduly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would be happy to handle this in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It is our position that it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll hear you in the morning tomorrow. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 0930 hours.
